eyebrow: SQL Dialects: T-SQL, PL/SQL, MySQL & Beyond · Chapter Four
subtitle: Lesson 21 · Joins, Subqueries & Set Operations

eyebrow: The problem a plain JOIN can't solve
code:
-- A plain JOIN's subquery can't see c.CustomerID
SELECT c.CustomerName, o.OrderID
FROM Customers AS c
JOIN (SELECT TOP 3 OrderID FROM Orders
      WHERE Orders.CustomerID = c.CustomerID) AS o
  ON 1 = 1; -- ERROR: c not in scope
caption: "Top 3 orders per customer" needs the subquery to know which customer.

code:
SELECT c.CustomerName, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate
FROM Customers AS c
CROSS APPLY (
  SELECT TOP 3 OrderID, OrderDate
  FROM Orders
  WHERE Orders.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
  ORDER BY OrderDate DESC
) AS o;
caption: CROSS APPLY lets the derived table see columns from earlier in FROM.

code:
SELECT c.customer_name, o.order_id
FROM customers c
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT order_id FROM orders
  WHERE orders.customer_id = c.customer_id
  ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 3
) AS o;
caption: Identical concept — only the keyword changes from APPLY to LATERAL.

code:
-- Oracle: LATERAL works...
FROM customers c, LATERAL (SELECT ... ) o

-- ...and so does CROSS APPLY, added for
-- easier migration FROM SQL Server
FROM customers c CROSS APPLY (SELECT ...) o
caption: Oracle hedges by supporting both, specifically to ease T-SQL migrations.
